projects.title: allacampingplatser.se
projects.subTitle: A fullstack application.
projects.name: allacampingplatser
projects.description: A comprehensive camping site discovery platform for Sweden that allows users to search, filter, and explore camping locations across the country. The application features an interactive map with location markers and clusters, detailed information pages for each camping site, and a responsive design that works seamlessly on both mobile and desktop devices. The platform integrates with Contentful CMS for dynamic content management and uses Mapbox for advanced mapping capabilities.
projects.shortDescription: An interactive map-based platform for discovering and exploring camping sites across Sweden with advanced filtering and search capabilities.
features: Interactive Map with Location Markers and Clusters
Responsive Design for Mobile and Desktop
Location Detail Pages with Rich Content
Hover Highlighting Between List and Map Views
Custom Animation Effects for UI Elements

caseStudy.problem: Camping information in Sweden is scattered across municipal websites, PDFs and forums — there was no single place to browse every campsite on a map, compare them and plan a trip. I wanted a product that solved a real discovery problem end to end, and that forced me to handle real-world constraints: geodata at scale, content operations, SEO and performance on mobile networks.
caseStudy.approach: I built it as a content-driven Next.js application. Every campsite lives in Contentful with a structured content model (location, facilities, imagery, seasonal info), which keeps the data editable without deployments. The frontend statically generates a page per campsite for SEO, while the map experience is fully client-side and interactive. The stack is deliberately boring where it should be — TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind — so the effort could go into the parts users feel: the map, the filtering and the speed.

craft.title: Map performance at scale
craft.text: Rendering hundreds of markers kills the frame rate on mobile, so markers are clustered and the map only renders what the viewport needs. Panning and zooming stay smooth even on mid-range phones.

craft.title: List ↔ map as one surface
craft.text: Hovering a campsite in the list highlights its marker on the map and vice versa, so the two views behave as one connected surface instead of two parallel UIs.

craft.title: SEO as architecture, not afterthought
craft.text: Each campsite gets a statically generated, indexable page with structured content from the CMS — the map is the experience, but the pages are what search engines and shared links land on.

craft.title: Two languages, one content model
craft.text: Swedish and English are handled through the CMS localization model rather than duplicated content, keeping translations in sync with a single source of truth.

caseStudy.outcome: The platform is live at allacampingplatser.se and in active use. [FYLL I: 2–3 verifierbara utfall — t.ex. antal campingplatser i databasen, organisk trafik/månad, antal indexerade sidor i Google Search Console, Lighthouse-poäng]
caseStudy.reflection: [FYLL I: vad du skulle gjort annorlunda — t.ex. val du omprövat kring datamodell, karta eller rendering. En ärlig reflektion väger tyngre än en säljande avslutning.]

projects.title: meetingtimecalculator.com
projects.subTitle: A focused SEO utility.
projects.tagline: Fair meeting times across time zones
projects.name: meetingtimecalculator
projects.description: A free, single-purpose web tool that finds the best meeting time for 2–10 participants spread across time zones. Each participant sets their timezone and working hours; a fairness-first algorithm ranks the top overlapping windows so no one is repeatedly stuck with a 6 AM or a 10 PM call. All calculations run in the browser using official IANA timezone data, so daylight-saving transitions are handled automatically and no participant data ever leaves the device. Results are shareable via a single link.
projects.shortDescription: A DST-safe meeting scheduler that ranks the fairest overlapping times for 2–10 people across time zones — entirely in the browser.
features: Automatic daylight-saving (DST) handling via IANA data
Client-side only — no data stored or sent

caseStudy.problem: Coordinating a meeting across time zones is deceptively hard: offsets shift with daylight saving, tools quietly favour one region, and the math gets worse with every participant added. Most existing converters answer 'what time is it there' but not the question people actually have — 'when can all of us reasonably meet?' I wanted to solve that specific job with a tool fast and honest enough that people would reach for it over a spreadsheet.
caseStudy.approach: I built it as a focused, SEO-first Next.js tool: statically prerendered for search and speed, with the entire scheduling engine running client-side so there's no server round-trip and no data leaves the browser. The core is a fairness-first algorithm that scores candidate slots across every participant's working hours instead of just intersecting them, and all timezone math is driven by official IANA data so DST transitions are correct by construction rather than by hand-tuned offsets. The scope is deliberately narrow — one job, done well.

craft.title: Fairness over naive overlap
craft.text: Rather than returning any shared slot, candidate times are scored so the cost of an awkward hour is spread fairly — the tool won't keep handing the same person the 6 AM call.

craft.title: DST correct by construction
craft.text: All conversions use IANA timezone data, so daylight-saving jumps are handled automatically — no manual offsets to drift out of date twice a year.

craft.title: Private by default
craft.text: The whole calculation runs in the browser. Nothing is stored or sent, which keeps it fast, cheap to run, and trustworthy for scheduling work conversations.

craft.title: SEO as the distribution model
craft.text: The page is statically prerendered and structured around the real questions people search — 'best meeting time for US and Europe' — so the tool is discoverable at the moment of need.

caseStudy.outcome: The tool is live at meetingtimecalculator.com. [FYLL I: 2–3 verifierbara utfall — t.ex. organisk trafik/månad, antal rankande sökord, Core Web Vitals/Lighthouse-poäng, användning per månad]
caseStudy.reflection: [FYLL I: en ärlig reflektion — t.ex. vad du lärde dig om att bygga för sök vs. för användare, eller vad du skulle förenkla/utöka i algoritmen eller U:t.]
